title: Neutopia
subtitle: Eight medallions across four worlds
summary: Neutopia is Hudson's overhead action-adventure, first released for PC Engine in Japan on 17 November 1989.
body: Neutopia is Hudson's overhead action-adventure, first released for PC Engine in Japan on 17 November 1989. The warrior Jazeta seeks eight stolen medallions and Princess Aurora, captured by the demon Dirth. The land is divided into four spheres, each containing places to explore and crypts to conquer. A charmed compass helps guide the search. The journey builds through small discoveries: another passage, a useful item or a conversation that gives the player a clearer idea of where to venture next.

Jazeta's expedition connects outdoor exploration with enclosed crypts where enemies and obstacles guard the medallions. Equipment and discoveries extend what he can accomplish, so returning to a previously seen place can reveal another possibility. The four spheres give the search a larger shape while keeping individual destinations readable. The princess and the medallions tie these separate journeys to a common purpose: recovering the powers that once maintained peace in Neutopia. Each completed crypt brings that restoration closer and prepares the player for a further part of the land.

The game reached North America on TurboGrafx-16 in April 1990. Its familiar overhead perspective and mixture of exploration, equipment and combat made it a clear alternative for players drawn to The Legend of Zelda's approach. Progress could be preserved through passwords or compatible backup memory, allowing the longer journey to continue across sessions. A sequel followed Jazeta's disappearance through the search undertaken by his son. Neutopia gave Hudson's console a sustained fantasy expedition alongside its more immediately arcade-oriented attractions.
